learning: No race data yet. Expected to learn whether kp=3 oscillates on the slalom and whether 1.6 base speed reaches the 1.5 m/s average needed for completion within 3 s.
notes: Baseline complete robot: Builder's neutral five-sensor geometry with a proportional-derivative line follower (kp=3, kd=0.3, small ki) at 80% drive and last-direction line recovery. Written before any race, so performance is unknown.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or earlier integration feedback. I kept the Builder's baseline geometry exactly (five sensors at y=0.04, x from -0.024 to 0.024, 12 mm footprints, track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg) so the controller is designed for that geometry. Sensor weights are the sensor's lateral position scaled to [-2, 2] (x/0.012, clipped), so a positive signal (tape on the left) steers left, as the contract requires. Sensor spacing of 0.012 m matches the 0.012 m footprint, so the tape always covers at least one or two sensors. kp=3 gives a maximum turn of 6 (about 2100 PWM of differential), which is strong enough for the bends without saturating. kd=0.3 damps oscillation from the 10 ms loop. ki=0.05 is small to avoid windup on long bends. base_speed=1.6 gives 80% PWM, which should reach the roughly 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3 s, leaving headroom for slowing on tight bends. line_loss='last_direction' keeps the robot turning toward the side it last saw the tape, which suits a line that leaves on one side. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with moderate line error. This is untested and will be revised after the race.
